To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the introduction of polar groups on position 3 of imidazole ring improves the water dispersibility and the dispersing power of the ionic liquid surfacts.
the presence of a methyl group in position 3, as well as the presence of a double bond, improves the dispersibility of SWNT in water.

the presence of a hydrophilic group in position 3 (i.e., a hydroxymethyl, an ethoxy, a hydroxyethyl, an ethoxymethyl, or an acetoxy group) of the imidazolyl ring of 1-hexade-cyl-3-vimBr increases the affinity of the ionic liquid toward the nanotube surface, as shown by the results of molecular dynamics simulations, and improves the SWNTs water solubility
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of dispersing agents for SWNTs in aqueous media.
the synthesis and characterization of novel water-dispersible ionic liquid-based surfactants and with the study of the interaction of these compounds with SWNTs.
the study of the influence of the chemical structure on the ability of the ILs to disperse SWNTs in aqueous solutions, with the aim of finding a suitable candidate as dispersant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the bromide anion, the alkyl group, the imidazole and the vinyl group in the 1-hexyl-3-viimBr structure are all necessary to obtain a stable aqueous dispersion of SWNTs.

the presence of a hydrophilic group in the imidazole headgroup of the ILs, such as a hydroxyl group, is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the dispersing ability in water, as also confirmed by MD simulations.
the introduction of the vinyl group in position 3 is the key to the dispersing capability of the ILs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of a polar headgroup, such as hydroxyl, is not necessary for the formation of SWNTs aqueous suspensions, but it is important for the stabilization of the dispersion, as well as the length of the hydrophobic tail.
the presence of a methyl group in position 2 of the imidazolyl ring, together with a vinyl group in position 3, is the best combination to achieve the highest SWNTs dispersing ability.

the introduction of a methyl group in position 3, with respect to the vinyl group, improves the water dispersibility, while the introduction of a hydroxymethyl group does not have a significant effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a hydrophobic group in the position 3 of imidazol rings is essential for the formation of stable SWNT dispersions, while the length and the structure of the hydrophobic group are not relevant.
the introduction of a methyl or an acetyl group at position 3 of imidazolyl ring, which is known to reduce the water-solubility of the IL surfactant, is able to increase the SWNT dispersibility.

the addition of a hydrophilic group at the 3-position of the imidazolyl ring of the surfactant, in particular a hydroxyl or a carboxylate group, leads to an increase in the affinity of the surfactants for water, but also to a decrease of their capability to disperse the SWNTs.
